attacks: A1 journal renamed/replaced with EMPTY file while owner live, owner exits, restart
A2 journal replaced with COPIED/STALE records (genuine but older chain)
A3 journal replaced with FOREIGN forged records
A4 journal name replaced with a SYMLINK
A5 control directory renamed/replaced between ATTEMPT fsync and transport call
A6 symlink swap at a base/control path component
A7 kill -9 mid-state (after ATTEMPT fsync), then restart
A8 two live processes contend for the capture
A9 inode recycling: freed journal inode number reused by a forged journal
A10 temp substitution between identity check and cleanup/finalize
A11 final substitution after verification, before COMPLETE

(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A1: FAILS — lock file replaceable/symlinkable (r2 defect); journal replacement invisible to the lock.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A10: FAILS — stat-then-unlink by pathname unlinks whatever the name denotes (r4 gap 3, same publication shape).
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A11: FAILS — single verification, then COMPLETE binds the name.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A2: FAILS — no content or identity binding on the journal at all.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A3: FAILS — forged records accepted if they parse.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A4: FAILS — journal open follows the pathname.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A5: FAILS — no control-dir pinning; the replacement dir is simply used.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A6: FAILS — pathname traversal follows swapped components.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A7: DETECTS — consumed-ATTEMPT semantics work only because the journal happens to survive untouched.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A8: DETECTS — works until the lock path is replaced or symlinked (r2: separate lock file follows symlinks / can be path-replaced).
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.A9: FAILS — no genesis/nonce binding; (dev,ino) or name alone is trusted.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.cannot_prove: Anything about the journal: the lock and the journal are different pathname objects; either can be replaced independently.
(a) pathname + flock on a separate lock.proves: Mutual exclusion only while the lock file's pathname keeps denoting the inode both processes flock.

(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A1: FAILS — r3 defect: empty-file replacement still splits; restart can treat the replacement as fresh history.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A10: FAILS — publication unchanged from (a) unless separately fixed (r3 fixed the rename overwrite via NOREPLACE, but not check/unlink substitution).
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A11: FAILS — COMPLETE binds after one verification; the window before COMPLETE is unguarded.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A2: FAILS — copied records on a new inode: without an external binding, copy vs original is undecidable at restart.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A3: DETECTS — schema/exact-key + record verification reject casual forgeries; a fully self-consistent forgery is undecidable (no external anchor).
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A4: PROVES — O_NOFOLLOW single open rejects the symlink (r3 PATH_TYPE).
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A5: FAILS — the journal fd survives, but nothing binds the control dir; post-replacement restart resolution follows the new dir.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A6: DETECTS — fd-relative opens after pinning help only if a dir fd was pinned; pure (b) opens the journal by path once.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A7: PROVES — held-fd journal + consumed-ATTEMPT restart semantics (r3 behavior).
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A8: PROVES — flock on the journal fd is a real single-owner token while held.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.A9: FAILS — (dev,ino) is the whole identity; a recycled number with forged records is indistinguishable.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.cannot_prove: Which inode is canonical after the owner exits: the lock dies with the process, and (dev,ino) comparison has no external anchor — an empty replacement IS a well-formed empty journal to a fresh opener that trusts the name.
(b) single journal fd + flock on the jou.proves: One writer at a time on ONE inode; appends never reopen by pathname; a replaced journal is a different inode than the locked one (JOURNAL_SPLIT detectable at open when (dev,ino) is compared).

(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A1: FAILS — modeled T1: live owner detects (HOLD to old inode), exits; restart opens the empty canonical journal as fresh and CALLS S1 AGAIN (DOUBLE_CALL + RESTART_IGNORED_CONSUMED).
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A10: FAILS — modeled T3 / r4 gap 3: _write_once_fd stats the temp inode then unlinks BY PATHNAME; substitution in the window unlinks a foreign inode.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A11: FAILS — modeled T4 / r4 gap 3: final verified once; substitution before COMPLETE lets COMPLETE bless a replaced final name.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A2: FAILS — modeled T1b: restart trusts the stale copy's records; consumed ATTEMPT/COMPLETE in the true journal ignored; S1 called again.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A3: DETECTS — schema strictness (r3) rejects malformed forgeries; self-consistent forgery undecidable without an external anchor.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A4: PROVES — modeled T1c: PATH_TYPE at fence and at restart.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A5: FAILS — modeled T2: no fence between ATTEMPT fsync and transport -> the call is issued into a replaced control dir (CALL_AFTER_CONTROL_REPLACEMENT); restart then follows the new dir and re-calls.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A6: PROVES — component-wise no-follow traversal + dirfd identity rechecks (r4 R2-07 lineage).
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A7: PROVES — modeled T7: restart reproduces ATTEMPT_CONSUMED_AMBIGUOUS, zero calls.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A8: PROVES — modeled T5: contender HOLD:OWNER_BUSY, zero mutation.
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.A9: FAILS — modeled T6: recycled inode + forged genesis-only journal is parsed as fresh; S1 re-called. (dev,ino) has no nonce/genesis anchor in (c).
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.cannot_prove: Restart truth after replacement across owner exit: fail() appends the HOLD to the still-open OLD inode, while a restart resolves the CANONICAL NAME — which may denote the empty replacement (r4 adjudication gap 1). Also cannot prove the pre-call window: r4 fences before the ATTEMPT append, not between ATTEMPT fsync and the call (gap 2).
(c) pinned directory fd + fd-relative op.proves: Live-owner exclusion and live detection: dir-fd flock before journal open, fd-relative appends, fence re-assertion catches replacement while the owner runs; temp fd held through finalize; NOREPLACE rename.

(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A1: PROVES — at restart: name's inode != binding, binding inode absent -> HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED, zero calls.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A10: FAILS — orthogonal: publication identity is not a journal-ownership property.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A2: PROVES — copy's inode != binding; binding inode found under its renamed entry -> HOLD:JOURNAL_RENAMED; never silently trusted.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A3: PROVES — forged records cannot reproduce the genesis hash + nonce held in the identity object.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A4: PROVES — the name must resolve to the binding inode as a regular file; a symlink is neither.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A5: DETECTS — restart resolves the control dir by binding (renamed dir found -> HOLD:CONTROL_REPLACED with truth located); a LIVE swap mid-run is not fenced by (d) alone.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A6: DETECTS — resolution compares inodes, so a swapped component yields a mismatch HOLD; traversal safety itself needs (c)'s no-follow walk.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A7: PROVES — verified journal reproduces consumed ATTEMPT -> AMBIGUOUS, zero calls.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A8: FAILS — alone: no mutual exclusion whatever.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.A9: PROVES — recycled (dev,ino) with forged genesis fails nonce + genesis_hash (modeled T6 under A).
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.cannot_prove: Anything DURING a run by itself: it has no lock (two live owners both pass open-time checks) and no fences (a swap after open is invisible until the next open). It is a restart-truth mechanism, not a live-ownership mechanism.
(d) identity/genesis binding (external i.proves: Open/restart-time authenticity and canonicity: the journal that may be trusted is the one whose (dev,ino) + nonce + genesis hash match an object the adversary's pathname games cannot rewrite (created O_EXCL, immutable, outside the control dir). Replacement, copying, and recycling all become DECIDABLE at restart.

(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A1: PROVES — empty file has no genesis/chain -> rejected at restart (modeled B/T1 PASS).
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A10: FAILS — orthogonal (publication), inherits pathname cleanup failures.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A2: FAILS — modeled B/T1b: stale genuine prefix verifies; restart ignores the true journal's later ATTEMPT+COMPLETE and calls S1 again.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A3: DETECTS — chain rejects lazy forgeries; a fully recomputed forged chain verifies (no external genesis anchor).
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A4: DETECTS — followed symlink's foreign content fails the chain (modeled B/T1c PASS via content, not type).
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A5: FAILS — modeled B/T2: no fence concept; call proceeds after replacement.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A6: FAILS — content says nothing about the path taken to reach the file.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A7: PROVES — modeled B/T7: chain-verified journal reproduces the consumed ATTEMPT.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A8: FAILS — modeled B/T5: no lock; contender acquires and calls.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.A9: FAILS — modeled B/T6: forged chain from a forged genesis is self-consistent; recycled inode trusted; consumed ATTEMPT ignored.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.cannot_prove: Canonicity/uniqueness: a hash chain proves a file is A valid history, never that it is THE history. A stale-but-genuine prefix chain verifies perfectly; two chain-valid journals can coexist (split-brain) with no rule to choose; and the genesis itself needs an external anchor or a fully forged chain verifies.
(e) content-addressed ownership (hash-ch.proves: Content authenticity and tamper-evidence of a GIVEN journal file: any record edit, reordering, or forgery that does not recompute the whole chain from a genuine genesis is detectable; a torn tail is classifiable (QFJ2 lineage).

(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A1: PROVES — modeled T1: live fence HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED; restart HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED; S1 called exactly once.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A10: PROVES — modeled T3: no unlink exists in the design; substitution -> HOLD:TEMP_SUBSTITUTED, foreign inode intact.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A11: PROVES — modeled T4: F-COMPLETE re-verification (inode + content hash) -> HOLD:FINAL_SUBSTITUTED, no COMPLETE appended.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A2: PROVES — modeled T1b: restart HOLD:JOURNAL_RENAMED (binding inode located, never trusted silently); zero re-calls.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A3: PROVES — genesis hash + nonce in the immutable identity object decide against any forgery.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A4: PROVES — modeled T1c: HOLD:PATH_TYPE live and at restart.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A5: PROVES — modeled T2: F-PRECALL fence HOLD:CONTROL_REPLACED, NO call; restart locates truth in the renamed dir, HOLD:CONTROL_REPLACED, zero calls.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A6: PROVES — component-wise O_NOFOLLOW traversal from the trusted parent + per-fence name->inode comparisons.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A7: PROVES — modeled T7: HOLD:ATTEMPT_CONSUMED_AMBIGUOUS, zero calls.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A8: PROVES — modeled T5: HOLD:OWNER_BUSY, zero calls, zero mutation.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.A9: PROVES — modeled T6: recycled inode number (identical (dev,ino)) rejected on nonce/genesis hash -> HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED.
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.cannot_prove: Kernel/filesystem compromise; an adversary who can rewrite the identity object before setup or the trusted parent itself; NFS semantics (out of platform assumption); availability (every attack still costs the capture a HOLD — the contract buys integrity with liveness, deliberately).
(f) COMBINATION — (c) pinned dir fd + fe.proves: The union, with each mechanism covering the others' blind spot: (c) gives live exclusion + live detection; the F-PRECALL fence closes the ATTEMPT->call window; (d) makes restart resolution decidable after ANY pathname replacement across exit; (e) makes record forgery/corruption decidable; OC-9/OC-10 make publication identity-bound and cleanup incapable of touching foreign state.

matrix: Design x attack outcome matrix for QF-YAHOO-REV3-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT-20261016-19 r5. Outcomes: PROVES = the design's mechanism decides the attack fail-closed by construction; DETECTS = attack is caught but a named weakness remains; FAILS = the attack defeats the design (a modeled trace or a lineage defect demonstrates it). Designs (a)-(e) are the candidate space; (f) is the recommended combination, modeled as A_CONTRACT.
recommendation: (f) — the combination, stated normatively in ownership_contract.json. No proper subset survives the matrix: (c) alone loses restart truth (A1/A2/A9) and the pre-call window (A5); (d)+(e) without (c) have no live ownership (A8) and no live fences (A5 live half); (e) alone cannot decide canonicity (A2); (a)/(b) are superseded lineage constructions whose failure modes r2/r3 already demonstrated in real fixtures.
